subject: maths
title: Area and Perimeter
seo_title: Year 5 Area and Perimeter Worksheets: Composite Shapes, cm² and m²
standard_text: Measure and calculate the perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes in centimetres and metres; calculate and compare the area of rectangles (including squares), and including using standard units, square centimetres (cm²) and square metres (m²) and estimate the area of irregular shapes.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 area and perimeter worksheets for the National Curriculum: perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes, area of rectangles with length × width in cm² and m², compound shapes, estimating irregular areas and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Perimeter: add every side. Area of a rectangle: length × width.
key_sub: Find missing sides first. Split composite shapes into rectangles and add their areas. Perimeter is in cm or m; area is in cm² or m².

faq.q: What do Year 5 children learn about area and perimeter?
faq.a: They calculate the perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes in cm and m, find the area of rectangles and squares with length × width in cm² and m², and estimate the area of irregular shapes.

faq.q: How do you find the area of a compound or composite shape?
faq.a: Split it into rectangles, find each area with length × width, then add them. You can also find the whole rectangle and take away the missing part.

faq.q: How do you estimate the area of an irregular shape in Year 5?
faq.a: Put it on a 1 cm squared grid. Count the whole squares and the squares that are half or more covered, and leave out the rest.

faq.q: What is the difference between cm and cm²?
faq.a: cm measures a length, such as a perimeter. cm² (square centimetres) measures an area: the number of 1 cm by 1 cm squares that fit inside a shape.

sets.title: Area of rectangles and squares (length × width)

items.q: This is a square. What is its area?
items.e: All the sides of a square are the same, so length and width are both 7 cm: 7 × 7 = 49 cm².

items.q: Which rectangle has the largest area?
items.e: Work out length × width for each: 10 × 3 = 30, 6 × 6 = 36, 8 × 4 = 32, 11 × 2 = 22. The largest is 6 cm by 6 cm (36 cm²). The longest perimeter does not always give the largest area.

items.q: Which rectangle has the largest area?
items.e: Work out length × width for each: 14 × 4 = 56, 9 × 7 = 63, 16 × 3 = 48, 10 × 6 = 60. The largest is 9 cm by 7 cm (63 cm²). The longest perimeter does not always give the largest area.

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area of a rectangle = length × width: 11 × 8 = 88 cm². 38 cm would be the perimeter.

items.q: This is a square. What is its area?

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 90 m². It is 15 m long. How wide is it?

items.q: A square has sides of 12 cm. What is its area?

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 48 cm². What is the length of the side marked ?

items.q: A rectangle is 20 m long and 15 m wide. What is its area?

items.q: Which rectangle has the smallest area?

items.q: You estimate the area of an irregular shape on a squared grid. Which squares do you count?
c: Whole and half or more covered
items.e: Count every whole square, and count a square as 1 if half or more of it is covered. Leave out squares that are less than half covered. The parts you count and leave out roughly balance.
Whole squares: 12. Squares half or more covered: 8. Estimate: 12 + 8 = 20 cm². Squares less than half covered (16) are not counted.

items.q: A wall is 5 m long and 3 m high. It has a door 1 m wide and 2 m high. What area of wall needs painting?
items.e: Wall: 5 × 3 = 15 m². Door: 1 × 2 = 2 m². Take away the door: 15 − 2 = 13 m².

items.q: George has 20 m of fence to make a rectangular vegetable patch. Which patch has the largest area?
items.e: All four use 20 m of fence. Areas: 9 × 1 = 9 m², 8 × 2 = 16 m², 7 × 3 = 21 m², 5 × 5 = 25 m². The square has the largest area.

items.q: A rectangle is 12 cm by 6 cm. A square has the same perimeter. What is the area of the square?
items.e: Perimeter of the rectangle: 12 + 6 + 12 + 6 = 36 cm. Side of the square: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm. Area: 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

items.q: A lawn is 9 m long and 6 m wide. New turf costs £4 per square metre. How much does turf for the whole lawn cost?
A rectangular field is 25 m long and 18 m wide. A fence goes all the way round, except for a gate 3 m wide. How much fence is needed?
items.e: Perimeter: 25 + 18 + 25 + 18 = 86 m. No fence across the gate: 86 − 3 = 83 m.

items.q: A football pitch is 100 m long and 64 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Length × width: 100 × 64 = 6,400 m².

items.q: Grace’s bedroom floor is a rectangle 4 m long and 3 m wide. What area of carpet does she need to cover it?
items.e: Covering a floor is area: 4 × 3 = 12 m².

items.q: A rectangular poster has an area of 600 cm². It is 30 cm wide. How tall is it?
items.e: Area = width × height, so height = 600 ÷ 30 = 20 cm. Check: 30 × 20 = 600 cm².

items.q: A square playground has a perimeter of 64 m. What is its area?
items.e: Each side: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 m. Area: 16 × 16 = 256 m².

items.q: A classroom floor is 9 m long and 7 m wide. What is the area of the floor?
items.e: Length × width: 9 × 7 = 63 m².

items.q: Jack’s family puts a fence round their rectangular garden. It is 15 m long and 8 m wide. How much fence do they need?
items.e: The fence goes along all 4 sides: 15 + 8 + 15 + 8 = 46 m.

items.q: Room A is 5 m by 4 m. Room B is 6 m by 3 m. Which is true?
items.e: Areas: 5 × 4 = 20 m² and 6 × 3 = 18 m², so A is larger. Perimeters: both 18 m.

items.q: A patio is 6 m long and 4 m wide. Square paving slabs are 1 m by 1 m and come in packs of 5. How many packs are needed?
items.e: Area: 6 × 4 = 24 m², so 24 slabs. 24 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 4. 4 packs are not enough, so 5 packs.

items.q: A lawn is 12 m by 8 m. In the middle is a square pond with sides of 3 m. What area of grass is there?
items.e: Lawn: 12 × 8 = 96 m². Pond: 3 × 3 = 9 m². Grass: 96 − 9 = 87 m².
Whole squares: 6. Squares half or more covered: 7. Estimate: 6 + 7 = 13 m².

items.q: A classroom display board is 120 cm long and 90 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Length × width: 120 × 90 = 10,800 cm². Tip: 12 × 9 = 108, then × 100.

items.q: A rectangular flower bed has a perimeter of 34 m. It is 11 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two long sides make 2 × 11 = 22 m. 34 − 22 = 12 m for the two short sides, so each is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m.

items.q: This is the plan of an L-shaped hall. What area of carpet covers the whole floor?
items.e: Split into two rectangles: 4 × 3 = 12 and 10 × 5 = 50. Total: 12 + 50 = 62 m².

items.q: Noah’s garden is 8 m by 6 m. Isla’s garden is 7 m by 7 m. Which garden has the larger area, and by how much?
items.e: Noah: 8 × 6 = 48 m². Isla: 7 × 7 = 49 m². 49 − 48 = 1 m². The perimeters are both 28 m, but the areas are different.

items.q: Ava is making a rabbit pen with an area of 36 m². It could be 9 m by 4 m or 6 m by 6 m. Which pen needs less fence?
items.e: Both have an area of 36 m². Fence: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 m and 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24 m. The square needs less fence.
